# crumbs

> Read what a running Flutter app captured, from an LLM agent or a CI script: HTTP traffic, logs, exceptions, debug dumps, in-app events, gate checks, database queries, cache operations and frame timings. Records sit in in-memory ring buffers, with an optional redacted JSONL timeline on disk, and are served as `crumbs_*` MCP tools and `crumbs:*` CLI commands on the `dowel` substrate.

**Stack**: Dart >=3.13, Flutter >=3.47. A `dowel` plugin: `CrumbsDowelProvider` adds the `crumbs:*` commands and `crumbs_*` MCP tools, which call `ext.crumbs.*` VM Service extensions inside the app. Production dependencies: the Flutter SDK, `dowel`, `logging`, `meta`. Crumbs adds no build-mode guard of its own, so guard the install with `if (kDebugMode)` (`crumbs:install` writes it): anyone who reaches the VM Service of a build that carries crumbs can read every buffer.

**Setup**:

```bash
flutter pub add crumbs
dart run crumbs crumbs:install        # scaffolds ./bin/dowel, registers the plugin, patches lib/main.dart
dart run crumbs mcp:install           # the `dowel` entry in .mcp.json; reconnect the MCP client after it
./bin/dowel start --device=chrome     # or macos, linux, windows, a device id
./bin/dowel crumbs:tail               # "No log records." on a fresh start is not an error
```

```dart
import 'package:crumbs/crumbs.dart';
import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart' show kDebugMode;
import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart';

void main() {
  WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();

  if (kDebugMode) {
    CrumbsPlugin.install();
    CrumbsPlugin.registerWatcher(ExceptionWatcher());
    CrumbsPlugin.registerWatcher(DumpWatcher());
  }

  runApp(const Placeholder()); // your app
}
```

## API

- `CrumbsPlugin.install()`: registers the `ext.crumbs.*` extensions and installs `LogWatcher`, which listens on `Logger.root.onRecord`, turns on `hierarchicalLoggingEnabled` and sets `Logger.root.level` to `Level.ALL`. Idempotent; call it before `runApp` (before `Magic.init` on a Magic app). `--dart-define=CRUMBS_DISABLE=1` (or `true`, `yes`) makes it a no-op; watchers and adapters registered separately still install.
- `CrumbsPlugin.registerWatcher(CrumbsWatcher)`: installs the watcher at once and does not deduplicate, so register each one once. Shipped: `ExceptionWatcher` (chains `FlutterError.onError` and `PlatformDispatcher.instance.onError`), `DumpWatcher` (chains `debugPrint`; installs only in debug builds unless `DumpWatcher()..allowInRelease = true` is set before `registerWatcher`, and the host guard allows the build), `FramePerfWatcher` (frame timings; `blocks` fill only while `FlutterTimeline` collection is on).
- `CrumbsPlugin.registerHttpAdapter(CrumbsHttpAdapter)`: an HTTP capture adapter; `CrumbsStore.pendingHttpCount` sums each adapter's `pendingCount`. `DioHttpAdapter` installs no interceptor: an app's own Dio interceptor calls `DioHttpAdapter.recordRequest(...)`. An adapter that holds a body as structured data runs it through `CrumbsRedaction.redactParameters` before stringifying it, and a string body through `CrumbsRedaction.redactBody` before truncating it: the store masks only JSON and form strings, and a cut JSON body no longer parses.
- `CrumbsStore`: the ring buffers. `recordX`, `recentX({limit})` (`recentLogs` also takes `minLevel`), the `onXRecord` broadcast streams, `setCapacity(cap, kind: CrumbsKind.x)` (500 per buffer by default; frame perf holds 3600 and has `setFramePerfCapacity`), `clear()`, `clearFramePerf()`, `pause()`, `resume()`, `resetForTesting()`.
- `CrumbsRedaction`: credential masking of HTTP records (`hideRequestHeaders`, `hideRequestParameters`, `hideResponseParameters`, `redactParameters`, `redactBody`) and the host text hook `redactor`, which runs over log, event, exception and HTTP text before buffering; a hook that throws drops the record.
- `CrumbsFileSink.start(directory:, maxFileBytes: 1048576, maxFiles: 8)`: the rotating JSONL timeline of redacted log, event and exception records. It throws a `FileSystemException` when the directory cannot be written.
- `CrumbsDowelProvider` and `followCursor` (`package:crumbs/cli.dart`): the provider dowel loads from `lib/app/_plugins.g.dart`, and the polling loop behind `--follow`.
- `MagicCrumbsIntegration.install()` (`package:magic_devtools/crumbs.dart`): the Magic HTTP adapter and the model, cache, event, gate and query watchers, after `Magic.init()`. Available only with a `magic_devtools` release built on crumbs; otherwise `crumbs:install` warns and skips it. Until that release ships, `MagicTelescopeIntegration` feeds `fluttersdk_telescope`, not crumbs, so the HTTP, event, gate, query and cache buffers of crumbs stay empty in a Magic app.
- MCP tools: `crumbs_tail` (logs, reads `ext.crumbs.console`), `crumbs_requests`, `crumbs_exceptions`, `crumbs_dumps`, `crumbs_events`, `crumbs_gates`, `crumbs_queries`, `crumbs_caches`, `crumbs_frames`, `crumbs_clear`.
- CLI commands mirror the tools by name, except: `crumbs_exceptions` has no command, and `crumbs:install` and `crumbs:files` (the timeline files) have no tool. Pause and resume are extensions with neither.

## Platforms

Any Flutter target that exposes a VM Service in a debug or profile build: Android, iOS, web, macOS, Windows and Linux. `crumbs:install` guards with `kDebugMode`, so profile and release builds drop crumbs; write `!kReleaseMode` by hand to keep profile builds. `CrumbsFileSink` writes through `dart:io`, so the timeline on disk needs a native target.

## Rules for agents

- Crumbs reads, it never drives. Exercise the app first (tapir, a test script or a person), then read what it recorded; an idle app proves nothing.
- An empty buffer is not a quiet app until its producer is known to be registered: logs need `package:logging` calls, exceptions need `ExceptionWatcher`, dumps need `DumpWatcher` in a debug build, HTTP needs an adapter, events, gates, queries and caches need the Magic watchers (a `magic_devtools` release built on crumbs), frames need `FramePerfWatcher`. The CLI's empty-buffer warning names the missing producer for every buffer but logs and timeline files.
- `crumbs_frames` always carries `livenessCounter`, the count of frames drawn. After driving the UI, empty frames with a counter that does not move mean no `FramePerfWatcher` is registered or the engine stalled.
- Records come oldest first, the newest last. Without `since`, `limit` keeps the newest N.
- Zero the buffers with `crumbs_clear` before a repro; do not clear when chasing a fault that already happened.
- Page logs and events with the `cursor` each read returns, passed back as `since` (CLI: `--since`, or `--follow` to keep polling). A `since` that is not an integer is refused with `invalidParams` (the CLI exits 3), never ignored.
- A read command exits 75 when the extension is not registered yet (the app is still booting, is a release build, has no crumbs, or has `CRUMBS_DISABLE` set): retry a few times, then check the build mode and the install.
- `********` is crumbs' credential mask, not the app's value. A host `redactor` that throws drops the record, so a missing line after a sensitive log call can mean a failing redactor.
- Exceptions are the errors that reach `FlutterError.onError` or `PlatformDispatcher.instance.onError`; a `try`/`catch` that swallows an error shows up only if the code logged it.
- Magic model events go to the model buffer, which no extension, tool or command serves; `crumbs_events` holds auth, database and gate-definition events.

## Docs

- [Getting started](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/getting-started/index.md): the overview of adding crumbs and wiring the watchers
- [Installation](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/getting-started/installation.md): requirements, `crumbs:install`, the build-mode guard, MCP wiring
- [Quickstart](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/getting-started/quickstart.md): from a fresh Flutter project to a first captured record
- [Buffers](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/getting-started/buffers.md): the ring buffers, their capacities and eviction
- [Redaction](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/getting-started/redaction.md): credential masking and the host `redactor`
- [File sink](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/getting-started/file-sink.md): the JSONL timeline on disk and how to read it back
- [Watchers](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/watchers/index.md): what each watcher and adapter captures and how to register it
- [FramePerfWatcher](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/watchers/frames.md): frame timings, block attribution and the liveness counter
- [MCP overview](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/mcp/overview.md): how the crumbs tools join dowel's MCP server
- [MCP setup](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/mcp/setup.md): the `.mcp.json` entry and the reconnect
- [MCP tool reference](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/mcp/tool-reference.md): input schema and response for every `crumbs_*` tool
- [Cursor and filters](https://anilcancakir.com/crumbs/docs/mcp/cursor-and-filters.md): `since`, `cursor`, `logger` and `type` on logs and events
